_: The home table of route places (16k type 10, standard 18): a stretch of a major road built as one place, its crossings and its road dressing, between built places or a built place and a city. A route place has no catalogue record; this row is its record, typed `classification.type: route-structure` (its type-recipes.json row, read by worldgen.place_type for the acceptance freeze). worldgen.blueprint.catalogue_ids() reads its ids. `structures[]` lists one structure of each route-structure kind the exemplar set proves and who builds it: `this-place` (laid in this place's layout with the modular-runs rules, decision 0115), `route-compile` (a stair, lip step or stepped ascent of world/sources/routes/route-structures.json, built by worldgen.compile_route_structures), or another place id (a ferry crossing inside a settlement). A kind not on this stretch is `pending: packet` with the stretch that holds it.

places.name: the Border road crossings below Greenspring

why.founding: The Border road was laid on a Dunmer line from Stormhold to Thorn. West of the Greenspring track it drops off the ridge into the river marsh.
why.siteAdvantages: The road keeps to the dry strip at the mountain foot and crosses water only where it must: two reaches of the river marsh, where the water stands up to a metre and a quarter deep.
why.occupantsMotive: The crossings have no residents. The people of Greenspring keep the planks in repair because their trade goes out along this road.
why.pressures: The marsh rots the piles in a few seasons. Greenspring has to keep replacing them.
why.wouldChangeIf: A stone causeway would replace the planks if anyone paid for one.

structures.pendingWhy: not on this stretch: it stands 480 m east of Greenspring inside the Two-Gate Bridge's ground, which places it when that place is built
not on this stretch: the Drowning Gate ferry serves the Gideon-Blackwood road and is built at Claywater Station

places.name: the Mere Neck on the Long road

why.founding: The Long road from Archon to Gideon crosses Middle Argonia on what firm ground it can find. Here that is a strip of ground between two meres, barely higher than the water.
why.siteAdvantages: The neck is the only dry line between the meres for a long way. For about fifty metres the mere covers the north half of the road, knee-deep and in places to the waist.
why.occupantsMotive: The neck has no residents. Travellers drove poles into both verges so that a walker can keep to the causeway when the water covers it.
why.pressures: Poles mark the causeway verge. A walker who strays off the causeway between them goes into deeper water.
why.wouldChangeIf: If the meres dried back, the poles would be left standing on dry ground. No traveller would replace them.

southwest.towards: the marsh track west of the neck
